blocks.prompt: 5 Solve the following trigonometric equation: \(2\cos^{2}x - 3\cos x + 1 = 0\)
blocks.explanation:
Ghaur se dekhiye: yeh \(\cos x\) mein quadratic equation hai. Agar \(\cos x\) ko \(y\) samjhein to yeh \(2y^{2} - 3y + 1 = 0\) ban jati hai, jo hum Grade IX se hal karte aa rahe hain.
Find kya karna hai? Principal solutions aur general solution.
Rule: middle term split kar ke factorise, phir har factor zero.
Plan: \(\cos x = \frac{1}{2}\) aur \(\cos x = 1\) alag alag hal karo, phir period \(2\pi\) jama karo.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(2\cos^{2}x - 3\cos x + 1 = 0\).
Maloom karna: principal solutions aur general solution.
Tareeqa: \(\cos x\) mein quadratic ko factorise karenge (middle term ko tor kar), phir har factor ko zero rakh kar basic equations hal karenge.

Middle term ko torein
\[2\cos^{2}x - 2\cos x - \cos x + 1 = 0\]
Kyun: humein aise do numbers chahiye jin ka product \(2 \times 1 = 2\) aur sum \(-3\) ho. Woh \(-2\) aur \(-1\) hain, is liye \(-3\cos x = -2\cos x - \cos x\).

Factorise karein
\[2\cos x(\cos x - 1) - 1(\cos x - 1) = 0\]
\[(2\cos x - 1)(\cos x - 1) = 0\]
Kyun: pehle do terms se \(2\cos x\) aur aakhri do se \(-1\) common nikala; dono brackets ek jaise ban gaye, to \((\cos x - 1)\) common nikal aaya.

Do basic equations
\[\cos x = \dfrac{1}{2}\ \text{ or }\ \cos x = 1\]
Kyun: do cheezon ka product zero tab hi hota hai jab un mein se koi ek zero ho.
Dhyan dein: dono values \(-1\) aur \(1\) ke darmiyan hain, is liye dono cases jaaiz hain; koi case rad nahin hota.

Jab \(\cos x = \frac{1}{2}\)
Cosine positive: quadrant I aur IV, reference angle \(\frac{\pi}{3}\).
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}\]
\[x = 2\pi - \dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{5\pi}{3}\]
Kyun: table se \(\cos\frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{1}{2}\); quadrant IV ka angle \(2\pi - \alpha\).

Jab \(\cos x = 1\)
\[x = 0\ \text{ and }\ x = 2\pi\]
\([0, 2\pi]\) mein; aam taur par \(x = 2n\pi\).
Kyun: cosine sirf circle ke shuru wale point (positive x-axis) par 1 hota hai. Is value ka quadrant wala joda nahin banta. \([0, 2\pi]\) band (closed) interval hai, is liye 0 ke saath \(2\pi\) bhi aata hai.

General solution
\(\cos x\) ka period \(2\pi\) hai:
\[\left\{2n\pi\right\}\]
\[\cup \left\{\dfrac{\pi}{3} + 2n\pi\right\}\]
\[\cup \left\{\dfrac{5\pi}{3} + 2n\pi\right\},\ n \in \mathbb{Z}\]
Kyun: dono cases ki families ka union. \(\{2n\pi\}\) mein 0 aur \(2\pi\) dono shamil hain.

Tasdeeq
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}:\ 2\cdot\dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{3}{2} + 1 = 0\]
\[x = 0:\ 2 - 3 + 1 = 0\]
Kyun: \(\cos\frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{1}{2}\) aur \(\cos 0 = 1\) rakh kar dono taraf zero aaya. \(\frac{5\pi}{3}\) ka cosine bhi \(\frac{1}{2}\) hai, to woh bhi theek hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Kitab mein Exercise 10.1 ke jawab chhape hue nahin hain. Is page ka har jawab hamara apna hai: qadam ba qadam hal kiya gaya, computer algebra system (sympy) se alag se check kiya gaya, aur ek solution book se bhi milaya gaya. Kitab ke examples ki tarah hum principal solutions \([0, 2\pi]\) mein aur general solution sets ke union ki shakal mein dete hain. Aap apna kaam yahan wale hal se mila kar dekh sakte hain.
